actorName: UK Modern Slavery Statement Registry — Delta Monitor

firstRunAnomaly.observed: First-ever qualifying run pushed 5 STATEMENT_UPDATED (billable) events instead of an all-free BASELINE_SNAPSHOT set.
firstRunAnomaly.investigationConclusion: Ruled out a code defect, a state-persistence bug, and a KV-store-naming collision (the named KV store's readCount:0 and createdAt exactly matching run-start time proved state was genuinely empty). Most parsimonious explanation consistent with all evidence: genuine duplicate rows for the same organisation+year within the source registry's own 10,401-row bulk CSV export.

knownRisks: Health-check cadence risk: the registry updates on an annual cycle, so daily automated health-check runs may often find zero new/changed statements once baseline is established — expected behavior given real-world update frequency, not a defect
